title: The bomb and its fuse
summary: One monster in R.E.P.O. attacks with a bomb, and the game models the bomb itself: a body on a spring, a fuse with a tip, a glow, fire and sparks, curves for burning down and a monologue.
body: One of the monsters does not attack with its hands. It carries a bomb, and the game models the bomb as a thing rather than an animation: the body hangs on a spring with a source and a target, so it swings while it is held.
The fuse is its own object. It has a tip and a glow with transforms of their own, and a parent for its particles, which is how the burning end can be a separate piece of the model.
It burns visibly. There are particles for fire and for sparks, so the fuse is not only a timer but something you can watch.

The burning is animated with curves. The glow, the stiffness of the fuse and how much it shrinks each have their own curve, so the fuse bends and wastes away as it burns rather than staying the same shape.
Both ends are sprung. The bottom and the top of the fuse have springs with their own sources and targets, which is why a fuse can whip about while it is being consumed.
The monster carrying it is sprung as well. Its head follows a target on a spring and its body turns on a rotation spring, so the whole encounter moves with weight rather than snapping between poses.

It talks through the whole thing. There is a talk source with springs above and below, and the monologue is broken up by idle and attack breakers that each choose a time between a shortest and a longest value, which is why the talking does not follow a fixed script.
It has head objects, a move offset and death effects of its own, and the encounter itself is directed: there is a director with a state of its own and units behind it.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the colour texture the game ships for the monster that carries the bomb, with the diagram alongside it showing how the fuse is put together.
What this entry does not tell you: how long a fuse burns, how much blast damage the bomb does, or how many bombs the encounter uses. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The bomb body hangs on a spring with a source and a target.
The fuse has a tip and a glow with their own transforms and a parent for its particles.
The fuse burns with fire and sparks.
Its glow, stiffness and shrinking each have their own curve.
Both ends of the fuse are sprung, with sources and targets of their own.

facts.claim: The monster has a head on a spring with a target and a rotation spring for its body.
It talks through a source with springs above and below, and its idle and attack breakers take a time between a shortest and a longest.
